title: DEFIBRILLATION/ CARDIOVERSION
src: PDF_003 p16-17 (original knowledge list skips number 5; renumbered sequentially)
knowledge: Verbalizes principles and reasons for defibrillation or cardioversion.
States standard and electrical safety precautions when defibrillating or performing cardioversion on a patient.
Verifies "shockable rhythms" on EKG and correlates with clinical state of patient.
Verbalizes joule settings used for defibrillation sequence as per PALS standard (Monophasic/Biphasic) ordered by physician.
Verbalizes correct call to “stand clear” of patient and bed prior to defibrillation.
States procedure modifications required if patient has a pacemaker.
States the age specific and culturally sensitive teaching required.
skills: Demonstrates placing patient on crash cart monitor.
Administers sedation as prescribed, if the patient's condition permits.
Demonstrates measures to decrease thoracic impedance.
For Cardioversion places defibrillator in ‘sync’ mode and verifies QRS complexes appear with R wave marker on monitor for correct synchronization.
Places paddles or hands-off electrodes in proper location and charges to appropriate joules required or requested.
Follows safety precautions during the procedure, ensuring that the patient and staff are safe prior to and during the delivery of shock(s).
Demonstrates use of defibrillator paddles for “quick look”.
Demonstrates methods to discharge defibrillator of unwanted charge.
Documents defibrillation on Code Blue Form.
Documents defibrillation/Cardioversion procedure to include patient preparation, treatment and response.
attitude: Recognizes safety precautions in performing defibrillation/cardioversion.

title: DIABETIC EMERGENCIES
knowledge:
Define and differentiate the following diabetic emergencies:
    Hypoglycemia
    Hyperglycemia
    Diabetic Ketoacidosis
    Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic Nonketotic Syndrome
List the clinical manifestations of diabetic emergencies
List the diagnostic evaluations and state its importance in managing diabetic emergencies
State the complications of diabetic emergencies, its prevention and appropriate management
skills: Demonstrate the assessment that includes the mental status of diabetic patient in the emergency department.
Demonstrate the steps of diagnostic evaluation of blood glucose level.
Demonstrate the steps in the administration of glucose parenterally.
Demonstrate evaluation of patient's response to emergency medical care rendered.
attitude: Identify the diabetic patient with confidentiality and be able to deal in a professional manner.
